title: Participles 6: Passive Past Short Form
description: The short form of the passive past participle: the predicative twin of the long form. Drop the final -ый and one of the doubled н to get the short form; it agrees in gender and number only (no case); the long-vs-short rule decides which form fits each slot.
descriptionRussian: Краткая форма страдательного причастия прошедшего времени: предикативная пара к полной форме. Отбрасываем конечное -ый и одну из двух -нн-, получаем краткую форму; согласование только в роде и числе (падежа нет); правило «полная или краткая» решает, какая форма стоит в каждом слоте.
intro: Everything so far attached to a noun. The short form does the opposite: it stands as the predicate, saying that the thing has been done rather than describing a thing that was. It drops a letter and loses its case forms entirely, keeping only gender and number. In one family the stress moves off the suffix as soon as an ending appears.
rules: The short form is the predicative form: it sits AFTER the subject as the complete predicate. Книга прочитана = the book has been read. The long form is the attributive twin: прочитанная книга = the read book.

Formation: take the long form, drop the final -ый, and for the -нный and -енный / -ённый families also drop one of the two н. The four endings are zero (masculine), -а (feminine), -о (neuter), -ы (plural).
Short forms agree with the subject in gender and number ONLY. They have no case forms. The four-form set (прочитан, прочитана, прочитано, прочитаны) is the whole inventory.

In the -ённ- family the stress migrates from the masculine -ё- onto the ending in the feminine, neuter, and plural: решён, but решена, решено, решены. Learners often keep -ё- by analogy and get it wrong.
examples: решён, решена, решено, решены (solved; stress migrates onto the ending in fem / neut / pl)
Книга была прочитана Машей. (The book was read by Masha.)
Школа построена в 1980 году. (The school was built in 1980.)

tables.title: Long form to short form: the four-form paradigm

items.prompt: Recap from L4: what is the passive past long-form participle of написать?
items.promptEnglish: Form the passive past long-form participle of написать.
items.hint: Recap: the -ать family takes -нн- + adjective endings.
items.explanation: Recap from L4: написа- + нн + ый = написанный (the long form, attributive). Today we will derive the short form (написан, написана, написано, написаны) by dropping -ый and one of the two н.

items.prompt: Take прочитанный and form the short masculine form.
items.promptEnglish: Form the short masculine form of прочитанный.
items.hint: Drop -ый and drop one of the two н: -нный → -н.
items.explanation: Прочитанный → drop -ый → прочитанн → drop one н → прочитан (short masculine). The single -н is the hallmark of the short form.

items.prompt: Книга _____ Машей. (The book was read by Masha.)
items.promptEnglish: Pick the short feminine form that fits the predicate slot.
items.hint: The slot is a predicate, and the subject (книга) is feminine. Which short form agrees?
items.explanation: Прочитана is the short feminine form, agreeing with the feminine subject книга. The slot is a predicate, so the short form is required (a long form would produce a sentence fragment).

items.promptEnglish: Pick the form that fits the predicate slot.
items.hint: The slot is a predicate; the subject (письмо) is neuter. Long forms cannot stand alone as a predicate.
items.explanation: Написано is the short neuter form, agreeing with the neuter subject письмо. The slot is a predicate ('the letter has been written'), so the short form is required.

items.prompt: _____ книга лежит на столе. (The read book lies on the table.)
items.promptEnglish: Pick the form that fits the attribute slot.
items.hint: The slot is an attribute (the participle modifies the noun). Which form fits inside a noun phrase?
items.explanation: Прочитанная is the long feminine form, attributive, agreeing with the feminine noun книга: 'a book that has been read'. The slot is an attribute (the participle sits inside the noun phrase), so the long form is required.

items.hint: Where is the participle: with the noun as an attribute, or AFTER the noun as a predicate? Which form belongs in which slot?
items.explanation: 'Книга прочитанная' puts the long form in a predicate slot, which is a fragment in modern Russian. The fix is the short form: 'Книга прочитана'.

fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Short feminine form in a predicate slot, with the agent (ветром) in the instrumental: the door has been opened by the wind.
hints: The slot is a predicate (no noun follows the participle); the subject (дверь) is feminine. Which form agrees?
explanations: Открыта is the short feminine of открытый, agreeing with the feminine subject дверь. The construction is a passive past predicate with an instrumental agent (ветром). Открытая is the long feminine (attributive only); открывшая is the active past feminine ('a woman who had opened'); открыт is the short MASCULINE form, wrong gender.

errorCorrection.explanation: A standalone predicate needs the SHORT form: 'Работа сделана'. The long form сделанная is attributive and, with nothing to modify, leaves a fragment. Сделана is the short feminine, agreeing with работа; сделан is masculine and сделано neuter.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: The open door creaked in the wind.
errorCorrection.explanation: Here the participle modifies дверь as an attribute (which door?The open one), so the LONG form is required: открытая. The short form открыта is predicative only and cannot sit inside a noun phrase before its noun. Открытое is the long neuter, wrong gender for the feminine дверь; открывшая is the active past ('a woman who had opened'), not the passive 'opened'.

Дело is neuter, so the short predicate form takes the neuter ending: решено. Решена is the short feminine and fits only a feminine subject (задача решена). Short forms agree in gender and number with their subject; решённое is the long form.

The participle modifies задачу as an attribute in the accusative (the direct object of получила), so it needs the LONG form in the feminine accusative: решённую. The short form решена is predicative and has no case forms, so it cannot sit inside a direct-object phrase. Решённая is the long feminine NOMINATIVE, the wrong case for an object; решённой is the genitive/dative/instrumental/prepositional feminine, also wrong for the accusative object slot.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: The exhibition was opened in May.
errorCorrection.explanation: With была the slot is a passive past PREDICATE, so it takes the short form: была открыта. The long form открытая is attributive and produces an ungrammatical predicate even with была. Открыта is short feminine, agreeing with выставка.

Школа is feminine, so the short predicate form takes the feminine ending: построена. Построен is the short masculine, agreeing only with a masculine subject (дом построен). Short forms agree in gender and number with the subject. Построено is the short neuter; построенная is the long form (attributive), not a standalone predicate.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: The problem has already been solved by the student.
errorCorrection.explanation: The short form drops one of the doubled н: short feminine of решённый is решена, with a single -н and end stress. Решённа keeps the long-form double -нн- and is not a valid short-form spelling. Решённая is the full long form (attributive); решено is the short NEUTER, wrong gender for the feminine задача.

minimalPairs.explanation: The slot is a predicate (Дверь is the subject; the participle is the complete predicate). The short form Открыта carries the passive past meaning predicatively. The long form Открытая is attributive and would leave only a noun-phrase fragment ('the open door'), not a complete sentence.

Both options are short forms, but they differ in gender. Письмо is neuter, so the short form takes the neuter ending: Написано (-о). Написана is the feminine ending (-а), wrong for a neuter subject. Short forms agree in gender and number only; there is no case marking to worry about.

reviewVocab.definition: short form (the predicative form of the passive past participle; sits as the complete predicate after the subject; agrees in gender and number only, no case)
reviewVocab.example: Книга прочитана; письмо написано; дверь открыта; задачи решены.

reviewVocab.definition: long form (the attributive form; sits with the noun as an adjective and agrees in gender, number, and case)
reviewVocab.example: Прочитанная книга — полная форма; в предложении «Книга прочитана» стоит краткая форма.

reviewVocab.definition: predicate (the slot the short form fills; the part of the sentence that says something about the subject)
reviewVocab.example: В предложении «Книга прочитана» слово прочитана — сказуемое; книга — подлежащее.

reviewVocab.definition: agreement in gender and number (the short form has no case forms; only the four endings: zero, -а, -о, -ы)
